LFM3 is our new generation of Liquid Foundation Models (LFMs), built to be the starting point for specialized intelligence. It brings text, vision, audio, omni, and decision models onto one shared backbone, all in the 2B parameter range. This means you can pick the model for your modality, fine-tune it on your own data on a single GPU, and deploy it where your application runs.

LFM3 brings four main changes compared to our previous LFM2 family:

LFM2 showed that a hybrid of short convolutions and attention can run fast on-device without sacrificing quality. For LFM3, we used our hardware-in-the-loop architecture search to redesign that architecture for agentic use cases, which need more capability per parameter and fast inference over long contexts. The search now covers 14 device and backend combinations, from phones and a Raspberry Pi 5 to laptops, cloud CPUs, GPUs, and the Qualcomm Hexagon NPU.

LFM3-1.7B-Base has 24 layers and four main changes:

The payoff shows at long context. Per parameter, LFM3-1.7B matches LFM2-1.2B on short prompts across edge devices, and with 8K tokens in context it is about 25% faster. LFM3-1.7B-Base was pre-trained on 22T tokens with the same 128K vocabulary as LFM2.5-8B-A1B . The final 3.5T tokens are a mid-training stage on curated data with a larger share of agentic traces and tool calls, which also extends the context window to 256K tokens.

Every LFM3 model branches from LFM3-1.7B-Base. Instead of running one large general-purpose model, you pick the one that fits your inputs, customize it, and run it on-device.

The vision and audio models also get two new in-house encoders:

Each model runs in transformers . The snippets below come from the model cards, which also list the other inference engines each model supports.

Reach for LFM3-1.7B when you need local agents, tool calling, structured outputs, or a base for domain-specific fine-tuning. It is post-trained to run in agentic harnesses such as Hermes Agent, Pi, and OpenClaw. It outperforms its predecessor, LFM2.5-2.6B, with 35% fewer parameters, and the biggest gains are on agentic tasks: on WebArena-Verified, it scores 38.42 against 3.02, and it even beats Qwen3.5-9B on long tasks in browsers and business apps. You can find more details in the LFM3-1.7B model card .

To run LFM3-1.7B, install the latest version of transformers :

For local agent setup, see the Agent Harnesses guide .

Reach for LFM3-VL-2B when you need on-device visual understanding. It is the first LFM vision model that takes video as input; it reasons step by step before it answers, and it finds objects and reasons about how they are placed, a strong foundation for robotics. Compared with LFM2.5-VL-3B, it has fewer parameters (1.9B against 3.1B) yet raises the average across 62 vision benchmarks from 57.6 to 71.4, on par with Gemma 4 12B, a model more than six times larger. You can find more details in the LFM3-VL-2B model card .

To run LFM3-VL-2B, install transformers>=5.21.0 with its vision dependencies:

See the LFM3-VL-2B model card for tool calling, tool search, and on-device inference with llama.cpp.

Reach for LFM3-Audio-2B when you need voice chat, speech recognition, speech synthesis, or translation across 18 languages on a laptop or edge device. It takes text or audio as input and responds with text, speech, or both, and it can turn spoken requests into tool calls. Compared with LFM2.5-Audio-1.5B, it uses a new in-house audio encoder and speech codec, speaks with higher quality (UTMOSv2 3.83 against 3.22), and adds audio understanding, general-purpose audio reasoning, and tool calling. You can find more details in the LFM3-Audio-2B model card .

To run LFM3-Audio-2B, install transformers>=5.20.2 with its audio dependencies:

Load the model and processor directly from the Hugging Face Hub:

Then ask a question aloud and get a reply in text and speech:

See the LFM3-Audio-2B model card for live speech recognition, speech synthesis, audio understanding, and tool calling.

Reach for LFM3-Omni-2B when you need one on-device model that sees, listens, and talks back, in place of a separate ASR model, vision-language model, LLM, and TTS model. It can answer spoken questions about an image, watch and listen to a video together, and turn what it sees and hears into tool calls. It is our first omni model, with text, vision, and audio input and both text and speech output, and it keeps the core capabilities of the standalone LFM3 models, including visual question answering, speech recognition, speech synthesis, and instruction following. Like LFM3-Audio-2B, it speaks through LiquidCodec, which turns generated tokens into speech faster than real time, so spoken replies stream as the model generates them. On audio-visual video understanding, it beats models up to 10.7B parameters, such as Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, on Daily-Omni, WorldSense, and AV-SpeakerBench. You can find more details in the LFM3-Omni-2B model card .

To run LFM3-Omni-2B, install transformers>=5.20.2 with its vision and audio dependencies:

Then ask a question about a photo by voice:

See the LFM3-Omni-2B model card for speech output, video with its soundtrack, and tool calling.

Reach for the d1 models when you need fast, structured decisions instead of generated text. Give them a situation (a support ticket, an invoice, an app screen, a photo, a voice note) and a list of questions, and they answer all of them in a single forward pass, each with a calibrated probability. Beyond yes/no, choices, and scores, they can now point at objects, read values from documents, estimate numbers with a range, and pick every option that applies. You can find more details in the model cards for d1-2B and d1-omni-2B .

To run d1-2B, install transformers>=5.19 with its vision dependencies:

Then load d1-2B and ask it several questions about one support ticket in a single pass:

For brevity, we only include the example for d1-2B. See the d1-omni-2B model card for audio clips and spoken questions.

LFM3 is built to be specialized. Frontier models are powerful generalists, but they are not necessarily experts in your use case. LFM3 packs extra capacity into a small, fast model, so a short fine-tune can turn it into a reliable expert on your task, with your data, terminology, and tools. Because it is small, you can deploy the fine-tuned model where your application runs, from devices to private infrastructure to the cloud.

Every model can be fine-tuned on a single GPU, and these notebooks walk you through a complete task for the text, vision, audio, and omni models, from data preparation to evaluation.

We adapt LFM3-VL-2B into three complementary robotics models for orchestration, navigation, and manipulation . The orchestrator operates a robot arm through tool calls: it grounds objects by pointing, measures them with depth tools, invokes motion planners, and checks outcomes in subsequent camera images. The navigator follows route descriptions using recent RGB observations, predicting spatial targets and a waypoint trajectory in just five tokens. The manipulation VLA maps images, language, and robot state to eight-step chunks of continuous actions in a single forward pass. Jointly trained across 15 embodiments, the VLA achieves 96.2% average success across the four LIBERO suites and 45.7% on RoboCasa-GR1 tabletop tasks, generating action chunks in under 50 ms on a Jetson AGX Orin with TensorRT FP16. These results highlight LFM3-VL-2B as a compact foundation for robotics, spanning high-level planning to low-level control with real-time action generation on embedded hardware.

Watch LFM3-VL-2B handle perception, navigation, and manipulation in this demo video .

All LFM3 models are open-weight and available on Hugging Face today:

Christophe Gleizes, 37, is a French journalist who specialises in African football for the Paris-based So Foot magazine

The plight of French sports journalist Christophe Gleizes, who is serving a seven-year prison sentence in Algeria, was highlighted at the Ballon d'Or ceremony.

Run by France Football magazine, the prestigious football awards were held in London where presenters Kate Scott and Thierry Henry dedicated the occasion to the 37-year-old reporter.

On a large screen behind them, it stated that he had been in jail for one year, three months and 27 days and alongside his photo was the hashtag "#FreeGleize".

He was arrested on a trip to Algeria where he had gone to report on a football club in Kabylie, a region where some people want self-determination. The authorities accused him of supporting terrorism.

"The Ballon d'Or France Football family would like to take this opportunity to dedicate this ceremony to Christophe Gleizes," said British broadcaster Scott and former Arsenal player and French striker Henry as the ceremony kicked off on Monday evening.

The event, held in London for the first time in its 70-year history, saw England and Bayern Munich strike Harry Kane crowned the world's top footballer of the year and London's City's Spanish midfielder Alexia Putellas taking the female prize.

Kane ends England's 25-year Ballon d'Or wait - how he bucked the trend

Putellas wins record-equalling third Ballon d'Or

Gleizes, who contributes to French magazines So Foot and Society, travelled to Algeria in May 2024 to report on Jeunesse Sportive de Kabylie (JSK), one of the country's best-known football clubs.

It is based in Tizi Ouzou, about 100km (62 miles) east of the capital Algiers, in the mountainous Kabylie region, which is mainly home to the ethnic Amazigh people (historically known as Berbers).

It is also the base of the Movement for the Self-Determination of Kabylie (MAK), which Algeria designated a terrorist organisation in 2021.

Gleizes was accused of possessing publications deemed harmful to national security.

The case centred on his contacts with a JSK official who was also associated with the MAK.

Reporters Without Borders (RSF), which has campaigned for his release, says the exchanges took place in a journalistic context and that some contacts predated the outlawing of the group.

During his appeal hearing last December, Gleizes acknowledged mistakes in his reporting and said he should have applied for a journalist visa rather than entering Algeria on a tourist visa.

"I beg your mercy so that I can be reunited with my family," he told the court.

Prosecutors argued that he had not travelled to Algeria to carry out journalistic work, but to commit a hostile act.

The Algerian authorities have yet to commented on the decision by the Ballon d'Or, which is organised by France Football magazine in partnership with European football governing body Uefa, to dedicate the ceremony to Gleizes.

RSF has announced a solidarity football match for 11 November, marking Gleizes's 500th day in detention, as part of its campaign calling for his release.

Former France internationals Robert Pirès and Vikash Dhorasoo, along with Paris Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire, are among the first participants announced.

Gleizes's case comes amid wider concerns over the prosecution and imprisonment of writers and other public figures in Algeria.

Franco-Algerian writer Boualem Sansal was sentenced to five years in prison for undermining national security before receiving a pardon from President Abdelmadjid Tebboune following mediation by Germany's president in 2025.

Gleizes's arrest also came during a period of heightened diplomatic tensions between France and Algeria, marked by the withdrawal of ambassadors and reciprocal expulsions of diplomats.

Relations deteriorated further after France recognised Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara in July 2024. Algeria supports the pro-independence Polisario Front, which seeks independence for the disputed territory.

As relations began to improve in May, France's Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin visited Algiers and urged the Algerian authorities to allow Gleizes to reunite "not with France, but with his mother".

He said that he believed President Tebboune would be receptive to the request.

Outcry after Algeria sentences French sports journalist to seven years in jail

'Welcome to 2976' - North Africa's Amazigh people ring in the new year

The tale of Algeria's stolen cannon and France's cockerel

How a massacre of Algerians in Paris was covered up

Umuhanzi Manzi Kalisi Daddy, uzwi nka Daddy Cassanova, yitabaje Urwego rw’Igihugu rw’Ubugenzacyaha (RIB), arusaba ubufasha ku kibazo cy’umuntu avuga ko arimo gukoresha izina rye mu kwamamaza igitaramo atabimuhereye uburenganzira.

Uyu muhanzi yagaragaje iki kibazo ku wa Mbere, tariki ya 26 Ukwakira 2026, abinyujije ku mbuga nkoranyambaga, asaba RIB kumugira inama ku nzira yakurikiza kugira ngo gikemuke.

Mu butumwa yandikiye uru rwego, Daddy Cassanova yavuze ko hari umuvangamiziki (DJ) ukorera mu Rwanda uri gukoresha izina rye mu kwamamaza igitaramo atigeze amwemerera.

Yagize ati: “Muraho, nitwa Manzi Kalisi Daddy, mu mwuga w’umuziki nkaba nzwi nka Cassa cyangwa Daddy Cassanova. Ndi umuhanzi nyarwanda ufite ubwenegihugu bw’u Rwanda na Canada. Ndifuza kubagezaho ikibazo cy’umu-DJ ukorera mu Rwanda uri gukoresha izina ryanjye mu kwamamaza igitaramo ntamuhaye uburenganzira. Ni izihe nzira nakurikiza kugira ngo iki kibazo gikemuke?”

RIB yamusubije imubaza niba yari yamaze gutanga ikirego. Daddy Cassanova yasubije ko itsinda rimuhagarariye ryamaze kohereza ubutumwa kuri email y’uru rwego, burimo ibimenyetso bifitanye isano n’iki kibazo.

Iki kibazo cyagaragaye nyuma y’uko uyu muhanzi atangaje ko atazitabira igitaramo yari yatumiwemo, giteganyijwe kubera ahitwa Atelier du Vin i Kigali ku wa 30 Ukwakira 2026.

Iki gitaramo cyateguwe na All Events Kigali, kikaba cyaratumiwemo abandi bahanzi n’abavanga imiziki barimo Logan Joe, Shemi, Kevin Klein, DJ Tyga na Joxy Parker.

MN202610_gnet936qnp.t:
Umunyamabanga Uhoraho muri Ministeri y’Ibikorwaremezo, Canoth Manishimwe, yatangaje ko mu mwaka wa 2025/2026, ingo 297, 068 zahawe amashanyarazi, zirimo izingana na 234,432 zahawe amashanyarazi afatiye ku muyoboro mugari na 62,636 afatiye ku mirasire y’izuba.

Yabiatangaje kuri uyu wa Kabiri tariki ya 27 Ukwakira 2026, mu kiganiro yagiranye n’Abadepite bagize Komisiyo y’Imiyoborere, Uburinganire n’Ubwuzuzanye bw’Abagabo n’Abagore.

Canoth Manishimwe yabagezagaho ingamba zitandukanye zigamije kwihutisha Gahunda ya Guverinoma yo Kwihutisha Iterambere mu cyiciro cyayo cya kabiri (NST2) by’umwihariko mu rwego rw’ibikorwa remezo.

Yatangaje ko hirya no hino mu gihugu, ubu abaturage bangana na 88.3% bamaze guhabwa amashayarazi yaba afatiye ku muyoboro mugari cyangwa afatiye ku mirasire y’izuba.

Yavuze ko mwaka wa 2025/2026, ingo 297, 068 zahawe amashanyarazi, zirimo izingana na 234,432 zahawe amashanyarazi afatiye ku muyoboro mugari na 62,636 afatiye ku mirasire y’izuba.

Muri gahunda ya NST2, Guverinoma y’u Rwanda yihaye intego ko mu 2029, amashanyarazi azaba yaragejejwe ahantu hose hari ibikorwaremezo by’iterambere no kugeza amashanyarazi mu Tugari twose, ari nako hongerwa uruhare rw’ingufu zisubira.

Guverinoma ivuga ko ibi bizagerwaho hongerwa imbaraga mu gukwirakwiza amashanyarazi hirya no hino mu Gihugu. Hakazibandwa ku nganda, inzu z’ubucuruzi, amashuri, ibigo by’ubuvuzi, n’ibindi bigira uruhare mu iterambere n’imibereho myiza y’abaturage.

Guverinoma ivuga ko izakomeza kongera ingufu zisubira kandi zidahumanya. Ibi ikavuga ko bizafasha kugabanya ikoreshwa ry’ingufu zikomoka ku bicanwa nk’inkwi, ibyatsi n’ibisigazwa by’ibihingwa n’ibindi.

Hazakomeza gutezwa imbere ubushakashatsi bugamije ikoreshwa ry’ingufu za nikereyeri mu nzego zirimo ubuzima, ingufu z’amashanyarazi, ubuhinzi n’izindi.

MN202610_4oxa9pq6qj.t:
Ahavuye isanamu, Screenshot Présidence RDC/X

"Sinumva ukungene umuntu yigeze kuyobora igihugu n'amamiriyoni y'abanyagihugu ashobora gutsindwa n'ishavu, bikamunanira kwifata, agafata ibirwanisho, akabihindukiriza kuri ba bantu yayobora imyaka 18 yose".

Aya ni amajambo ya Perezida Felix Tshisekedi avuga ku wo yasubiriye, Joseph Kabila, aherutse gutangaza ko ari we arongoye urunani rushasha rwa poritike na gisirikare, rwashinzwe mu ntango z'uku kwezi kugira ngo rurwanye ubutegetsi bwa Kinshasa, rusubiriye AFC/M23.

Mw'ijambo yashikirije inama y'abashingamateka b'urunani rwiwe ruri ku butegetsi mu mpera z'indwi iheze, Perezida Tshisekedi yavuze ko adatangazwa no kubona Kabila ava mu gacerere, akavuga ariko ko akoreshwa n'Urwanda.

Kuva uno muhari mushasha utangajwe ku mugaragaro, ni bwo bwa mbere umutegetsi wa Repuburika ya Demokarasi ya Congo ( RD Congo) agize ico ashikiriza ku mugaragaro, haba kw'ishingwa ryawo canke kuri Joseph Kabila.

Reta y'Urwanda nta co iravuga kuri aya majambo ya Perezida Tshisekedi.

BBC yasavye umushikiranganji w'Urwanda ajejwe imigenderanire n'ayandi makungu, Olivier Nduhungirehe, kugira ico ashikirije, ariko akaba yishuye mu butumwa bugufi ati "ntabwo twahora dusubiza ibyo Tshisekedi avuga ku Rwanda".

Mw'ijambo ryiwe, Perezida Tshisekedi, atarya umunwa, yagirije igihugu c'Urwanda na Perezida Paul Kagame akirongoye kugira uruhara mu ntambara ibera mu buseruko bwa Congo, kandi ko ari co kiriko gikoresha Kabila.

Ku bwiwe, ishingwa ry'umuhari FRN ni amayeri y'Urwanda mu ntumbero yo kwereka amakungu ko ari ingorane y' Abanyekongo ubwabo, akavuga ko ari inkurikizi z'ibikorwa vya diporomasi vya reta arongoye, vyo kwerekana ingene Urwanda ari rwo rupfukamye mu nda igihugu ciwe, vyatumye rufatirwa ibihano.

Ati: "Ni co gituma rwaciye rusaba umukozi warwo yakorera mu gifuri gusohoka kugira ngo afate ubuyobozi bw'ubu bugizi bwa nabi, kuko vyari ngombwa guha ico kibazo ishusho y'uko ari ikibazo c'abanyekongo ubwabo.

"Vyabaye ngombwa rero ko ava mu bwihisho, afata ibintu mu minwe, kugira ngo yerekane ko ari ikibazo kiri hagati y'abanyekongo. Imana ishimwe, nta n'umwe atabibona.

"Mbere ikintu canshimishije kuruta ibindi ni uko abenegihugu bacu, baba abanyapolitike canke abanyagihugu basanzwe, bose hamwe bahurije ku kwiyamiriza ivyo bikorwa."

Tshisekedi abona ko Kabila yahemukiye igihugu n'abenegihugu yigeze kurongora, kandi ko ari icerekana ko mu kiringo c'imyaka 18 yamaze arongoye igihugu ata rukundo yigeze agirira igihugu na beneco.

Yongeyeko ati: "Kuko iyo ukunda igihugu n'abanyagihugu baco, ntushobora kuja mu bintu nk'ivyo. Jewe nifatiyeko akarorero, nanje narabaye mu bihe nk'ivyo: igihe twarwanya intwaro z'agahotoro zitandukanye zigeze kuba muri iki gihugu, nta na rimwe twigeze twiyumvira gufata ibirwanisho ngo turwanye igihugu cacu."

Ku wa 12 z'uku kwezi kwa Gitugutu(10), ni ho hatangazwa ku mugaragaro ishingwa rya FRN kandi ko irongowe na Joseph Kabila , mu ntumbero yo gushira hamwe ico uno muhari mushasha wise "inguvu zo guhangana" kugira ngo urangize ico wise ubutegetsi bw'agahotoro no gushiraho umurongo mushasha wa poritike y'igihugu.

Imbere y'uko Perezida Tshisekedi agira ico ashikirije kuri Kabila na FRN yiwe, reta ntiyari bwigere ishikiriza ku mugagararo aho ihagaze, uretse bamwe mu banyaporitike bakorana na yo bagiye banegura ingingo ya Joseph Kabila yo kurongora uno muhari wasubiriye AFC/M23.

Eka n'Ububirigi, igihugu cahoze kirongoye RD Congo mu gihe c'ubukoloni, bwariyamirije ishingwa ry'uno muhari, aho Maxime Prévot , umushikiranganji w'imigenderanire, yavuze ko "bibabaje cane" kubona umuntu yahoze arongoye igihugu akaba na we nyene muri ico gihe yarahuye n'ingaruka z'imirwi yitwaje ibirwanisho ahitamwo "kuba indongozi y'umurwi wa politike na gisirikare urondera gushika ku butegetsi ukoresheje ibirwanisho".

MN202610_12mz9vqs6ck.t:
Nearly 5,000 healthcare workers have been trained to deal with Ebola

As fears grow that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo could spread further, Kenya, which announced its first Ebola case three weeks ago and has since had eight more cases, is hoping for the opposite.

Nine cases and two deaths have so far been confirmed.

With the first 20 of the people who came into contact with the first Ebola patient being released, the government has described it as a "milestone worth celebrating".

The government expects the outbreak to be declared over in less than two months, if efforts to contain the spread holds. But that is assuming there are no more cases, including from the 98 people still in quarantine and due to be freed next week.

Despite the initial release of the people in quarantine, Kenya's Health Director-General Patrick Amoth has reiterated that the focus was "firmly on the finish line".

The outbreak can only be declared over after 42 days from the time the last confirmed patient twice tests negative for Ebola, he said on Monday.

"We cannot afford to drop our vigilance until we reach that point," he said

In the days after the first case was announced, concerns had been rising that the virus could start spreading further, even as the government sought to assure citizens.

The US warned it citizens against travelling to Kenya, while neighbouring countries such as Uganda, Ethiopia and Somalia remain on alert.

Concerns remain among Kenyans that the disease could still spread more widely.

Nearly 5,000 people have died since Ebola was confirmed in DR Congo in May, making it the second most deadly outbreak of the disease.

With more than 10,000 cases in DR Congo, Kenya faces a steady risk of new cases arriving across borders, according to the International Rescue Committee, which has been working alongside both governments to contain the spread.

The latest outbreak has been caused by the Bundibugyo species, which is relatively rare, with no approved vaccine or treatment - though trials are under way.

Kenyans raised questions from the outset, about how the first patient was able to spend time in the region worst-affected by Ebola, then travel to two more countries before his illness was identified . He died days after his arrival in Kenya.

As a regional transport hub, the risk of the outbreak spreading remains a big concern.

The doctors' union in Kenya expressed concerns at "lapses" at various border points, including with neighbouring Uganda and Tanzania, as well as at Kenya's main airport.

Dennis Miskellah, the union representative, told the BBC that border and port facilities were grossly understaffed.

In the latest update on Monday, Amoth says that "each milestone brings us closer to the end of this outbreak, and together we will get there".

When the first case was announced, the authorities urged people not to panic, assuring them of heightened surveillance at airports and border crossings.

Kenya has since introduced enhanced screening for travellers arriving from 10 countries it considers to be at high risk: DR Congo, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, Angola, Zambia, Ethiopia, South Sudan and the Central African Republic.

Travellers arriving from those countries are required to complete a digital surveillance form before boarding their flights, and to present a QR code to port health officials on arrival.

Kenya also ordered enhanced public health screening of aircraft arriving from those countries, as authorities seek to prevent further imported cases.

Within the country, the government has been sharing public messages to create awareness about Ebola, including encouraging people to promptly report any suspected cases and seek care at a hospital.

It has also focused on hygiene and safety measures, such as washing hands and avoiding close contact with sick people.

The government has additionally designated treatment and isolation facilities across the country, and health workers have been trained to deal with the disease.

Amoth also said that a dedicated laboratory had been set up at the Kenyatta National Hospital Infectious Disease Unit to handle Ebola tests, to ensure that the hospital's laboratory was not contaminated.

Kenya has increased screening at border points

Following confirmation of the first Ebola case on 6 October, the health ministry conducted "robust contact tracing of anyone who may have been exposed", the World Health Organization (WHO) says. By 22 October, all contacts had been traced, both in Kenya and internationally, and placed in quarantine, it adds.

The government says that the confirmed cases so far are connected and there is no evidence that the virus has spread to the community.

Earlier, the International Rescue Committee noted that with all of those infected having links to the first victim, it showed Kenya's early response was working.

The government has been working with international partners, including Africa CDC and the WHO to support its response, including surveillance, communication and community engagement.

A toll-free emergency hotline, 719, has been provided to the public to report suspected symptoms.

Amoth earlier said that none of the contacts of the first patients had showed symptoms before going into quarantine "and therefore the potential to spread to another person is very minimal, literally non-existent".

The incubation period for Ebola ranges from two to 21 days, meaning those exposed to the virus may not become ill for several weeks. The Ebola virus spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.

Despite that, Kenya's health ministry said nearly 5,000 healthcare workers have been trained to deal with Ebola at the national and local levels, besides the facilities that have been designated to handle the virus.

The ministry urged people to remain calm and vigilant. It also asked Kenyans not to stigmatise people identified as contacts of Ebola cases.

The ministry, along with the WHO, have produced posters to help people understand Ebola and support its containment. One message reads: "Stop stigma, choose support. Stigma can discourage people from reporting symptoms or cooperating with response teams."

In addition, the government has procured supplies of protective equipment.

Not according to the Kenya Medical Practitioners and Dentists Union (KMPDU).

With three health workers and a hospital cleaner among those infected, questions have been asked as to whether the government could do more to protect workers.

Health workers and carers can face a higher risk of Ebola infection because caring for infected patients may bring them into contact with blood and other bodily fluids.

Questions remain over Ebola patient who travelled across three nations undetected

What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult?

Dennis Miskellah, the KMPDU deputy secretary general, told the BBC that protective equipment should be provided to hospitals so that they were fully protected, especially in case patients with symptoms do not declare that they have been in areas with Ebola.

He suggests the government ought to conduct proper health education to destigmatise the virus, so that people do not seek to hide their symptoms.

The International Rescue Committee also called for continued funding for contact tracing, border screening and training of frontline health workers in Kenya.

Kenya remains open with no restrictions on travel, trade or public gatherings.

Despite confirming nine cases, the authorities have explicitly ruled out a national lockdown or general travel ban for Kenyans.

The US on 19 October issued an advisory asking citizens to reconsider travelling to the country over Ebola concerns. Other countries have issued health alerts, including the UK, which warned its citizens that they may encounter enhanced health screening, and Canada, which has asked citizens to monitor their health for 21 days.

No country has issued an outright ban against their nationals visiting Kenya, nor have Kenyans been blocked from entering other countries over Ebola fears.

Kenyan authorities have ruled out travel restrictions

Analysts have raised concerns over the potential impact of public health fears on international travel and tourism but there is no evidence this has happened yet.

But the situation could change if the outbreak were to spread into the wider population.

The exact number of Kenyans living in the DR Congo is not clear.

A report authored last year by the Centre for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) think-tank put the number of Kenyans living in eastern DR Congo at about 2,500, including about 50 investors. It also noted that there were about four times as many Congolese living in the Kenyan capital, Nairobi, alone.

The Kenyan embassy in the Congolese capital, Kinshasa, which represents Kenya's interests in four countries - DR Congo, Central African Republic, Congo-Brazzaville and Gabon - has in the past urged Kenyans living in the region to formally register so that it is able to serve them better.

Several countries in the region have announced tightening of surveillance measures and enhanced screening for visitors.

One man who came into contact with the man who died in Kenya is under quarantine in Somalia and samples have been sent to Kenya for testing.

Somalia has also said it was taking precautionary measures, including enhancing surveillance measures at border points "given the evolving regional situation and the movement of people between countries".

In Tanzania, visitors are expected to undergo daily health monitoring for 21 days, through an automated tracking system, which was announced after Kenya confirmed multiple cases of Ebola infections.

Uganda later said 60 people who were being monitored after coming into contact with the Kenyan patient had all been discharged.

Uganda had reported two Ebola deaths shortly after the outbreak was reported in DR Congo, but the WHO has since declared it to be free of the disease.

On 20 October, Nigeria confirmed a case of Ebola in a female patient who travelled from Uganda to Abuja. Nigeria is the first West African state to report a case linked to the current Ebola crisis in East and Central Africa.

The woman, a 42-year-old Ugandan-born national is a wife of a Swiss diplomat who had travelled to the Ugandan capital for a holiday.
